lines.text: Poems as pictures.
Photos, follows and novels.
Stats only you can see.
Here's what's new in InkBoard.

lines.chapter: Share a poem as an image
lines.text: Chapter one. Share a poem as an image.
Every public poem now has a Share as image button.
Pick a design: Page, Ink or Board.
Story size fills a phone screen. Chat size fits a message.
Want just a few lines? Choose them, and the picture shows only those.
Every picture prints a short link back to the poem.
Chapter two. Profile photos.
Writers can now use a photo instead of an avatar.
Choose a picture, then drag or zoom to crop it.
It shows on your section of the board, and on your author page.
Chapter three. Follow an author.
Readers can follow the writers they like.
When a new poem or a new chapter goes up, a notification arrives.
More from the same writer joins that notification, quietly.
Chapter four. Novels, for writers.
Start a novel with a title, a language and a status.
The blurb is like the back of a book: readers see it first.
Upload a cover, and crop it to the shape of a book.
Write each chapter here. The Drop cap button gives it a large first letter.
Publish chapters one at a time, and move them into order.
Chapter five. Novels, for readers.
Novels sit on the board as book cards.
Each one has its own page, with the blurb and the chapters.
Chapters open with the writer's drop cap.
Ewe, Twi and Ga keep every letter and tone mark.
On a phone, Text settings change the size and the font.
Come back later, and InkBoard remembers where you stopped.
Save a whole novel to read offline, or follow it in a feed reader.
Chapter six. Private novels.
A novel can be private, with one password for the whole book.
Readers still see the title, the cover and the chapter list.
Unlock it once, and every chapter opens.
Chapter seven. Share a passage.
At the end of a chapter, tick the paragraphs you want to quote.
Trim the start and the end, sentence by sentence.
The count keeps you under 600 characters.
And the passage becomes a picture, ready to share.
Chapter eight. Stats for writers.
Stats shows how many devices follow you,
how often your shared links were opened,
and the words and reading time of each novel.
Every number is explained. No page views, no tracking: only what InkBoard already keeps.
That's what's new. Start writing free at tryinkboard.elabo.me
